args.summary: checkout-api failed health checks following the v2.3.1 deploy. Per runbook, rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback verification: service healthy across all regions, error rate 0.2%.
args.title: checkout-api rollback to v2.3.0 after v2.3.1 health check failures

trace.final:
Done. Here's what I did:

1. **Reviewed deployment history** for checkout-api: v2.3.1 (production) was unhealthy; the most recent healthy production release was v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc was only in staging and also unhealthy, so it was not a candidate).

2. **Rolled back** checkout-api to **v2.3.0** in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rollout succeeded and required no additional approval.

3. **Verified health**: all regions now running v2.3.0, service is healthy with a 0.2% error rate.

4. **Opened SEV2 incident** INC-0001 ("checkout-api rollback to v2.3.0 after v2.3.1 health check failures") documenting the failure and the rollback; the on-call engineer has been paged.

transcript.reasoning_content: Most recent healthy in production: v2.3.0. Rollback to v2.3.0, then open incident. Rollback first, then incident can be opened in parallel? Incident describes what I did — better after rollback succeeds. But they're independent-ish; incident depends on rollback outcome description. I'll do rollback first, then incident.
